hero.headline: Deposition Summary Services — You Send the Transcript, We Send the Summary
hero.subheadline: Some firms want software. Some want the work done. This is the second one. Send a transcript and get back a cited summary in the format your motion practice actually uses, without adding a seat, a login, or a new process for your paralegals to learn.

sections.heading: What You Get Back
paragraphs: Every summary is cited to the page and line it came from, so anything in it can be checked against the transcript in seconds. That is the part most outsourced summaries get wrong: they read well but cannot be verified, so someone ends up re-reading the transcript anyway.

You choose the format. Page-line summaries for motion practice and impeachment. Issue-based summaries when you need the testimony organised by theory of the case rather than by chronology. Narrative summaries when the summary is going to a client or an expert rather than to a judge.

The work runs on the same engine as our software, which means the summary you receive as a service is identical to the one you would produce yourself in the platform. Firms often start here and move to the software once they see the output, or run both: services for overflow, software for everyday volume.

sections.heading: Who This Is For
paragraphs: Firms with uneven deposition volume. If you take forty depositions one month and four the next, hiring for the peak is expensive and hiring for the average means missing deadlines. Per-page pricing means you pay for the forty and nothing for the four.

Firms where the bottleneck is not skill but hours. Your paralegals can write an excellent summary. The question is whether that is the best use of the day when the alternative is intake, client contact, or discovery responses.
Litigation support vendors and court reporting agencies who want to offer summaries to their own clients without building the capability in-house. We work behind the scenes on a white-label basis.

sections.heading: Pricing
paragraphs: Per page, not per seat. Standard summaries start at $0.06 per page, dropping to $0.008 per page at volume. There is no minimum commitment, no per-user licence, and no feature gating between tiers.

A typical 200-page deposition transcript therefore costs a few dollars to summarise rather than the several hundred dollars of paralegal time it displaces. Full pricing tiers are published on our pricing page, because we think a services page that will not tell you the price is wasting your time.

sections.heading: Confidentiality and Compliance
paragraphs: SOC 2 certified and HIPAA compliant. A BAA is available before any protected health information is uploaded, which matters when deposition exhibits include medical records.

Your transcripts are yours. They are not used to train models, and they are not shared with other clients. For firms that need it, our managed services team can build the whole workflow inside your own environment so the documents never leave your control.

faq.question: How is this different from your deposition summary software?
faq.answer: The software is a platform your team logs into and runs themselves. The service is us doing the work and sending it back. Same engine, same output quality, different amount of your team's time involved. Firms with steady volume usually prefer the software; firms with spiky volume or no spare paralegal hours usually prefer the service.

faq.question: What format do you need the transcript in?
faq.answer: Whatever your court reporter gave you. PDF, including scanned or image-based PDFs, plus TXT, DOCX, and the common transcript formats. If it is scanned rather than digital text, our OCR handles it as part of the same job at no extra step.

faq.question: Can I ask for a specific summary format?
faq.answer: Yes. Page-line, issue-based, narrative, or a firm template you already use. If you send us an example of a summary your firm likes, we match that structure rather than imposing ours.

faq.question: Do you handle exhibits and medical records attached to the deposition?
faq.answer: Yes. Exhibits are summarised alongside the testimony, and medical exhibits can be turned into a chronology at the same time. If the deposition is medical-heavy, our medical chronology services cover that side of the file.

faq.question: Is there a minimum volume?
faq.answer: No. One transcript is a valid job. Per-page pricing means there is nothing to commit to and nothing wasted if your volume drops.

faq.question: Who reviews the summary before it comes back to me?
faq.answer: Every summary carries page-line citations so your own team can spot-check any statement against the transcript quickly. We recommend that check on the first few jobs. It is faster than reading the transcript and it tells you exactly how much verification you need going forward.
